solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What banks account for every individual

blocks.note: 'Eh?' = 'What?', asking someone to repeat
AC is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A remark about how banks keep a separate account for every customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the opening of a question, but here it is an exclamation asking someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means every individual one taken separately.

clue.text: Spring practice in bare feet, footwear for summer?

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
drill = repeated practice
FEET without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone training barefoot in spring and wondering what to wear on their feet come summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare feet' reads as a scene detail, but it is an instruction to strip FEET down to EE, which then holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a light canvas rope-soled shoe worn in summer; the question mark flags that it is an example.

clue.text: Coach service of use during strike [in] capital

blocks.note: a coach is a railway carriage, or car
ACAS, the Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, mediates UK industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A coach company running a replacement service during a strike in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British government body that steps in to settle strikes, which is why a 'service' used 'during strike' is those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Caracas is one capital city, Venezuela's.

clue.text: Further crimes DA laid on Irishman

blocks.note: Aidan is an Irish name, as in the Irish monk St Aidan
taken as printed
to lay money is to bet it; laid = bet

explanation.surface: A district attorney pinning further crimes on an Irish suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Further' is a verb here, to help crimes along, and 'DA' is not the attorney but just the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid and abet is to help a crime along, so to further crimes.

clue.text: Fertiliser put on south of island wiped out reptile species

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
guano is bird or bat droppings used as fertiliser
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Fertiliser spread on the southern part of an island killing off a local reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiped out' seems to describe what the fertiliser did; it belongs to the definition, marking the reptile as extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a dinosaur, a reptile species long since wiped out.

clue.text: Most influential Davos summit has finished early

blocks.note: Davos is in the Swiss Alps, so its summit is an alp
HAS without its last letter

explanation.surface: The most influential delegates' meeting at the Davos summit wrapping up ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The Davos summit is the World Economic Forum, but here it is literally a mountain peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpha member of a group is the dominant, most influential one.

clue.text: Having second decision-making structure in case of dissent, the Westminster way

indicators.note: the rest sits inside the case

blocks.note: having = owning
S is the abbreviation for second
a decision tree is a branching diagram for making choices
the outer letters of DISSENT

explanation.surface: A government keeping a fallback decision process in case of dissent, as Westminster does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is used in its sense of a road: Downing Street is the Westminster street where the Prime Minister lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street is a street, a way, in Westminster, home of the Prime Minister.

clue.text: Smile, and date in the audience waves from the side

blocks.note: to beam is to smile broadly
to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A performer smiling at a date sitting in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's beam is its side, so a beam sea is one striking the vessel side-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam sea is a sea whose waves strike a ship at right angles to its keel, from the side.

clue.text: Facial hair you shouldn’t have? Say no more

blocks.note: 'You shouldn't have!' is a way of saying thanks, and ta is British slang for thanks
sh! tells someone to stop talking

explanation.surface: Someone being told, tactfully, that a moustache was a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' reads as disapproval of the moustache, but it is what you say on receiving a gift, a thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Tash is British informal for a moustache.

clue.text: One newly risen, standard planet waning in the east

indicators.note: VENUS shrinks at its east, the right-hand end of an across entry

blocks.note: par = the standard or normal level
VENUS losing its last letter

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: a planet newly risen, then fading low in the eastern sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly risen' sounds like a star or planet, but it describes a person who has risen socially.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone who has recently risen to wealth or position, an upstart.

clue.text: Man on top first, change lady under him liked initially

indicators.note: change the order of the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
the first letter of LIKED

explanation.surface: A racy line about a woman beneath a man who liked it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately suggestive; 'on top' really means on top of Everest, which Hillary first reached with Tenzing Norgay in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: in 1953 Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first to stand on Everest's summit, so 'on top first' pins him down.

clue.text: Fruit trees one foot, two feet or more?

blocks.note: a paw is an animal's foot
the plural, for two or more feet

explanation.surface: A question about how tall fruit trees grow: a foot, two feet, more?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' and 'feet' look like measurements of height; they are animal feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawpaws are tropical fruit trees, also called papayas.

clue.text: Educate minors, running teaching programmes?

indicators.note: the letters are set running into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A school running educational programmes for children.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that documentaries only teach loosely; they are an example of programmes that inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentaries are factual programmes meant to inform and teach.

clue.text: Sleep with tatty blankets left dirty and damp

blocks.note: to bed someone is to sleep with them
tatty = ragged
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Sleeping under shabby blankets that have been left filthy and damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blankets' looks like bedding in the scene; it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled means wet, dirty and untidy.

clue.text: Writer returning only some of one’s Biros

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following words

blocks.note: the letters spanning oNE'S BIros

explanation.surface: A writer handing back only a few of the pens he borrowed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, which makes a writer returning them a neat picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright.

clue.text: Spin gets Diane named for office

indicators.note: the letters are spun into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A PR campaign that gets Diane nominated to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests political PR, fitting a candidate being named for office.
explanation.definitionFit: Designate after a title (chair designate) means appointed but not yet in office.

clue.text: Tie families forged across fence in the middle

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
the middle letter of FENCE

explanation.surface: Two families forging a bond across the fence that divides their gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' is a sporting fixture, as in a cup tie, not a bond; the families never feature in the answer except as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a cup tie, a knockout match one round before the final.

clue.text: Powerless factory mobilised human element

indicators.note: remove P, the abbreviation for power

blocks.note: PLANT without P
anagram of HUMAN

explanation.surface: A factory hit by a power cut, with the workforce mobilised instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human element' reads as a phrase about people; only 'element' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanthanum is a chemical element, a rare-earth metal.

clue.text: Tasteless, absolutely not a sausage

blocks.note: naff is British slang for tacky or tasteless
all = completely, as in 'all wrong'

explanation.surface: Verdict on a dish: bland, and nothing at all like a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a sausage' and 'naff all' are both British slang for nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff all means nothing at all, which is what 'not a sausage' means.

clue.text: Large hunter chasing game lasts for one hour

indicators.note: take the last letters of the next words

blocks.note: tig is the British playground chasing game also called tag
the last letters of ONE and HOUR

explanation.surface: A big-game hunter chasing his quarry for a full hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lasts for one hour' reads as a duration; 'for' is just part of the instruction, and only ONE and HOUR supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a large predatory cat, a big hunter.

clue.text: Put a funny face on ghastly card

blocks.note: grim = ghastly
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Drawing a silly face on a terrible greetings card.
explanation.walkthrough: To grimace is to twist your face, which is a verb, so the definition 'Put a funny face on' must be read as a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, read as a verb: to grimace is to pull a twisted, comic or pained expression.

clue.text: Shared understanding lumberjack’s work, receiving down payment

indicators.note: something receiving a guest takes it inside

blocks.note: a lumberjack fells trees
down = low
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A lumberjack agreeing to work in return for a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down payment' looks like a single phrase meaning a deposit, but it must be split into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow feeling is sympathy or understanding shared between people.

clue.text: Music[’s] what gets punk going in old age

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the first letter of PUNK
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A pensioner's musical taste: what gets a punk moving in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old age' reads as one phrase but splits into O and ERA, with P slotted between.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: opera is one kind of music, drama set to song.

clue.text: Drug was introduced to hospital

blocks.note: to be introduced to someone is to meet them
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A drug brought into a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced to' suggests smuggling something in; it means met.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal abbreviation: meth is the street name for methamphetamine.

clue.text: Issue chap had going behind wife’s back

indicators.note: to go behind something is to follow it

blocks.note: the last letter of WIFE
chap = man
had dinner = ate dinner

explanation.surface: Trouble brewing over a man carrying on behind his wife's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun, a problem; the answer is a verb, to issue forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its verb sense: whatever issues from a source flows out of it.

clue.text: After taking everything off, grand party game

blocks.note: a net figure is what is left after all deductions
a ball is a grand dance party

explanation.surface: A party game played after everyone has stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking everything off' suggests undressing; it means deducting, as in net pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team ball game, widely played in Britain and the Commonwealth.

clue.text: Ship’s computer voided floppy in good time, twice each orbit?

blocks.note: HAL 9000 is the computer aboard the spaceship in 2001: A Space Odyssey
the outer letters of FLOPPY
in good time = early

explanation.surface: A spaceship's computer, its floppy disk wiped, still keeping time on each orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: One orbit of the Earth round the Sun is a year, so twice per orbit is every half year.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-yearly means twice a year, and a year is one orbit of the Sun.

clue.text: That woman’s daughters drive together

blocks.note: that woman's = her
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother's daughters sharing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive together' suggests a car pool; it means to round up animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cattle or sheep are gathered and moved as a group by a herder.
